\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{سارق} (sāriq)}{سارق (sāriq)}]{\ar{سارق} (sāriq) — a robber}

\label{lesson:AR-C321-sariq}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to give news, then the Arabic for to clarify.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{سارق}}
\textbf{\ar{سارق}} — \emph{sāriq} — \textquotedblleft{}a robber\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ركض} \ar{السارق} \ar{بين} \ar{السيارات}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rakaḍa as-sāriq bayna as-sayyārāt.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The robber ran between the cars.
\end{quote}

Plural \ar{سارقون}. \ar{لص} is the everyday word; \ar{سارق} is the one who stole.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{سارق}} (\emph{sāriq}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{s-r-q} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to take a thing secretly\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Sāriq} is its active participle, \textquotedblleft{}one who steals\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sāriq}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sāriq}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rakaḍa as-sāriq bayna as-sayyārāt.} — The robber ran between the cars.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to give news, then the Arabic for to clarify, then say \emph{sāriq} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{سارق} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A robber\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{نشال} (nashshāl)}{نشال (nashshāl)}]{\ar{نشال} (nashshāl) — a pickpocket}

\label{lesson:AR-C321-nashshal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to clarify, then the Arabic for a robber.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{نشال}}
\textbf{\ar{نشال}} — \emph{nashshāl} — \textquotedblleft{}a pickpocket\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{سرق} \ar{نشال} \ar{محفظتي} \ar{في} \ar{الحافلة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{saraqa nashshāl miḥfaẓatī fī al-ḥāfila.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A pickpocket stole my wallet on the bus.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{نشال}} (\emph{nashshāl}) is usually traced to the native Arabic root \emph{n-sh-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to snatch out quickly\textquotedblright{}. The \emph{faʿʿāl} pattern names someone who does a thing as his trade.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nashshāl}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nashshāl}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{saraqa nashshāl miḥfaẓatī fī al-ḥāfila.} — A pickpocket stole my wallet on the bus.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to clarify, then the Arabic for a robber, then say \emph{nashshāl} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{نشال} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A pickpocket\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{عصابة} (ʿiṣāba)}{عصابة (ʿiṣāba)}]{\ar{عصابة} (ʿiṣāba) — a gang, a band}

\label{lesson:AR-C321-isaba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a robber, then the Arabic for a pickpocket.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{عصابة}}
\textbf{\ar{عصابة}} — \emph{ʿiṣāba} — \textquotedblleft{}a gang, a band\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{اعتقلت} \ar{الشرطة} \ar{عصابة} \ar{من} \ar{خمسة} \ar{رجال}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{iʿtaqalat ash-shurṭa ʿiṣāba min khamsat rijāl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police arrested a gang of five men.
\end{quote}

Also a bandage or headband: one root, \textquotedblleft{}what binds\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{عصابة}} (\emph{ʿiṣāba}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-ṣ-b} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to bind round\textquotedblright{}. Lane gives \emph{ʿiṣāba} as a band tied round the head, and as a band of men bound together.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿiṣāba}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿiṣāba}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iʿtaqalat ash-shurṭa ʿiṣāba min khamsat rijāl.} — The police arrested a gang of five men.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a robber, then the Arabic for a pickpocket, then say \emph{ʿiṣāba} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{عصابة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A gang, a band\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{سلب} (salaba)}{سلب (salaba)}]{\ar{سلب} (salaba) — to rob, to snatch away}

\label{lesson:AR-C321-salaba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a pickpocket, then the Arabic for a gang.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{سلب}}
\textbf{\ar{سلب}} — \emph{salaba} — \textquotedblleft{}to rob, to snatch away\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{سلب} \ar{رجلان} \ar{المسافر} \ar{في} \ar{الطريق}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{salaba rajulān al-musāfir fī aṭ-ṭarīq.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Two men robbed the traveller on the road.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يسلب}, \emph{yaslub}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{سلب}} (\emph{salaba}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{s-l-b} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to strip a man of his clothes or goods\textquotedblright{}; \emph{salb} is taking away, and so \emph{salbī}, negative.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{salaba}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{salaba}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{salaba rajulān al-musāfir fī aṭ-ṭarīq.} — Two men robbed the traveller on the road.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a pickpocket, then the Arabic for a gang, then say \emph{salaba} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{سلب} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To rob, to snatch away\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{نهب} (nahaba)}{نهب (nahaba)}]{\ar{نهب} (nahaba) — to loot, to plunder}

\label{lesson:AR-C321-nahaba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a gang, then the Arabic for to rob.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{نهب}}
\textbf{\ar{نهب}} — \emph{nahaba} — \textquotedblleft{}to loot, to plunder\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{نهب} \ar{اللصوص} \ar{المحلات} \ar{في} \ar{الليل}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nahaba al-luṣūṣ al-maḥallāt fī al-layl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Thieves looted the shops in the night.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{ينهب}, \emph{yanhab}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{نهب}} (\emph{nahaba}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-h-b} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to take as plunder\textquotedblright{}; \emph{nahb} is spoil.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nahaba}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nahaba}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nahaba al-luṣūṣ al-maḥallāt fī al-layl.} — Thieves looted the shops in the night.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a gang, then the Arabic for to rob, then say \emph{nahaba} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
